name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia with Recurrent Genetic Anomaly
aliases: Acute myelogenous leukemia with cytogenetic abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of AML with recurrent genetic abnormalities

criteria.description: Presence of ≥20% myeloblasts in bone marrow or peripheral blood
Detection of specific recurrent genetic abnormalities such as t(8;21)(q22;q22), inv(16)(p13q22), or t(15;17)(q22;q12)
Immunophenotypic evidence of myeloid lineage by flow cytometry

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: ≥20% myeloblasts in marrow or blood plus presence of a recurrent genetic abnormality
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing by karyotyping, FISH, or molecular methods is essential for classification.

pathognomonic.notes: Presence of blasts in peripheral blood is characteristic
searchTerms: low blood counts with immature cells
reduced blood cells with blasts in blood

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bone marrow hypercellularity with myeloid blast proliferation
searchTerms: bone marrow crowded with immature myeloid cells
high myeloid blast count in marrow
pale skin and tiredness from anemia
fatigue and pallor due to low red blood cells

common.symptomName: Easy bruising and petechiae from thrombocytopenia
searchTerms: easy bruising and small red spots
petechiae and bleeding from low platelets

common.notes: Increased susceptibility to bacterial and fungal infections
searchTerms: recurrent infections due to immune weakness
infections caused by low white blood cells

common.notes: May reflect leukemic process or infection
searchTerms: temperature rise with no infection found

occasional.notes: Less common in AML compared to lymphoid leukemias

rare.symptomName: Central nervous system involvement with neurological deficits
searchTerms: nerve deficits due to CNS involvement
lung problems from blood cell buildup

imaging: Chest X-ray may show leukostasis-related infiltrates
CT or MRI if CNS involvement suspected
genetic: Cytogenetic abnormalities such as t(8;21), inv(16), t(15;17)
other: Bone marrow biopsy showing hypercellularity with >20% blasts
Flow cytometry confirming myeloid lineage markers (CD13, CD33)

distinguishingFeatures: Dysplastic changes in marrow with <20% blasts
Absence of recurrent AML genetic abnormalities

redFlags: Signs of leukostasis (respiratory distress, neurological deficits)
Severe bleeding or disseminated intravascular coagulation
references: WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues, 5th Edition, 2017
National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Guidelines for AML, Version 4.2023
Orphanet: Acute myeloid leukemia with recurrent genetic anomaly (ORPHA:98277)
